text:
maria: FYI ran a focused profile on TP all-reduce this morning. Seeing weird latency spike for ~8-32KB per-GPU messages. Baseline compute looks fine but all-reduce takes ~2-3x expected time. :thinking:

maria: dump of step-level latencies (tp=4, pipeline stages=2):
```
step 100: compute 18.2ms | allreduce 42.7ms | total 63.5ms
step 101: compute 17.9ms | allreduce 41.2ms | total 60.3ms
step 102: compute 18.4ms | allreduce 123.9ms | total 142.7ms  <-- spike
step 103: compute 18.1ms | allreduce 44.0ms | total 62.1ms
```

maria: attaching nccl topo/proto flags we used and the profiler timeline snippet. Looks like ping-pong behavior — some ranks wait longer, others busy.

kai: can you paste the nccl version + env? any TREE vs RING override? :eyes:

maria: NCCL 2.14.3, default coll algorithm (auto), no NCCL_TREE_COLL set. env: NCCL_DEBUG=INFO, NCCL_ASYNC_ERROR_HANDLING=1.

maria: repro command: `python perf/run_tp_profile.py --tp 4 --micro-batch 1 --seq 2048 --msgsize-sweep 4K,8K,16K,32K --repeat 200`

ash: my hunch is small-message inefficiency from a combination of: kernel selection (small GEMM vs fused kernels), and fragmented KV cache evictions creating many tiny reduce payloads. We saw similar pattern in a cache-coalescing bug earlier.

jing: uploaded a trace flamegraph (snippet):
```
|-- forward_stage_0 (18ms)
|   |-- matmul_fwd_small (11ms)
|-- allreduce (120ms)  <-- majority in ncclSend/ncclRecv wait
|-- forward_stage_1 (18ms)
```

jing: note the allreduce latency correlates with number of KV cache misses during prefix assembly. If the batcher emits 6 tiny KV updates instead of 1 coalesced chunk, we trigger more small-message traffic.

perf-bot: automated profile summary: TP allreduce median=46ms, p95=128ms, p99=210ms for msgsize range 4-32KB. Ring vs tree simulation suggests tree helps <16KB.

kai: interesting — NCCL's ring has lower bandwidth at tiny messages due to per-hop overhead; tree can reduce latency by logN hops but loses for large messages. So threshold tuning could be helpful. Also check chunking alignment: we chunk at 128KB by default; with these small payloads chunking may produce extra metadata overhead.

ash: actionable ideas:
- coalesce KV cache writes at batcher stage so reduces are single larger messages
- try forcing NCCL_TREE_COLL for msgsize <= 16KB in our runtime kernel selector
- lower the chunk size for RP (reduce packer) to avoid creating many small fragments in certain layouts

maria: I tried a quick experiment: enabled NCCL_TREE_COLL via NCCL_COLLNET_P2P_DISABLE=1 (local env toggle) and bumped chunking threshold to coalesce up to 48KB. Results (same workload):
```
before: allreduce median 46ms p95 128ms
after:  allreduce median 22ms p95 45ms
```

maria: caveat: for larger msg sizes (>=256KB) tree mode regresses a bit (~1.1x slower), so we'd need dynamic switching.

kai: do we have a cheap way to detect topology+msgsize and pick algorithm? NCCL has `ncclGetCollAlgo` internals but not public. We could implement heuristic: if per-request payload < X and num_ranks>2 then prefer TREE. Also check if link bisection or high-diameter fabrics change threshold.

jing: +1 on heuristic. Also adding a small async reduce thread to coalesce bursts from KV cache might hide latency without changing NCCL. E.g., buffer tiny KV updates for up to 1ms or until 64KB threshold then issue reduce. That trades a tiny extra latency for fewer allreduce ops.

ash: tradeoffs: coalescing delays can hurt tail latency for 1-off requests. Maybe make it adaptive: if queue depth low, don't wait; if bursty, coalesce. Our batching heuristics already have burst detectors — we can reuse them.

maria: noted. Also found a regression in commit a1b2c3d: it changed `reduce_chunk_align` from 64B to 4KB to help large models, but caused many tiny fragments for the KV layout we use. Reverting that for TP path improved steady-state.

kai: can you open a small PR to expose the algo threshold as a runtime/default flag? I'll try injecting a tree-for-small patch and run the CI perf suite.

maria: opened draft PR #3426 with the heuristic + config flag `tp_allreduce_algo_threshold_bytes` (default 32768). Results in PR description.

jing: I'll add a microbenchmark to perf harness to sweep thresholds per topology class (fat-tree vs torus) so we can populate a tuned table.

ash: also test overlapping by moving KV pack earlier in the stage to give compute more time to overlap with allreduce. small refactor but could reduce visible ping-pong.

perf-bot: scheduled nightly job: perf/tp/allreduce_threshold_sweep on 4xA100 cluster. ETA 12h.

maria: thanks all. Next steps: @kai try the tree toggle + chunk-align revert on your repro infra, @jing add microbenchmark, @ash add adaptive coalescer draft. I'll follow up with updated traces tomorrow. :thumbsup:
